places.name: Cafe de la Presse
places.description: A corner brasserie and newsstand facing the Chinatown gate, serving classic and modern French plates from breakfast onward. It suits an easy daytime meal, a glass of French wine on the terrace, or a relaxed early dinner close to Union Square.

places.name: JouJou
places.hours_note: Bar and raw bar open at 4:00 PM, Tuesday to Sunday, with happy hour until 6:00 PM.
places.description: A recently opened French restaurant from the team behind Lazy Bear, built around a seafood and raw bar. A good pick for a polished dinner in the Design District when you want French cooking with a lighter, shellfish-forward bent.

places.name: Verjus
places.hours_note: Full menu until 10:00 PM; bar snacks until 11:00 PM Fri and Sat. Closed Thanksgiving, Nov 26. Walk-ins welcome; reservations open one week ahead.
places.description: A Jackson Square cave a manger pairing a deep French wine list with small plates and plats du jour. It works well for an unhurried evening of wine and French plates a short walk from the Financial District.

places.name: Bon Delire

hours.sat: 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM
hours.sun: 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM

places.hours_note: Happy hour Monday to Friday, 3:00 to 5:00 PM. Lunch Thursday and Friday; brunch Saturday and Sunday; dinner from 5:00 PM.
places.description: A modern Parisian-style bistro at the water's edge on Pier 3, right by the Ferry Building. The most convenient French dinner or weekend brunch for a resident of 181 Fremont.
places.desk_note: Its site shows lunch on Thursday and Friday only, its booking page shows every weekday. Confirm lunch by phone.

places.name: Atelier Crenn
places.hours_note: Dinner only, about three hours at the table. Its site does not publish hours.
places.description: Dominique Crenn's poetic, seafood-forward French tasting-menu restaurant, the city's most celebrated French fine dining. Reserve it for a milestone dinner when the evening itself is the point.
places.desk_note: Hours are not published anywhere official. Confirm the evening and the booking by phone.

places.name: Chapeau!
places.hours_note: Times shown are the reservation window. Open Thanksgiving Day, Nov 26, noon to 8:30 PM. Closed July 4, Dec 25, Jan 1.
places.description: A husband-and-wife-run Parisian bistro on Clement Street since 1996, known for escargots, cassoulet and coq au vin. A dependable, warm neighborhood French dinner when you want tradition over novelty.
places.desk_note: The times are when tables can be booked, not when it closes.

places.name: Routier
places.hours_note: Walk-ins welcome. Parties over six book by email.
places.description: A stylish neighborhood bistro at California and Divisadero serving a changing, ingredient-driven French menu. A strong choice for a relaxed French dinner in Pacific Heights, with parties over 6 handled by email.
places.desk_note: The phone number comes from the Michelin Guide, not its own site.

places.name: Boulevard
places.description: Nancy Oakes' long-running Belle Epoque dining room on the Embarcadero, serving seasonal Californian cooking with a classic polish. Among the easiest upscale dinners to reach from 181 Fremont, and a natural business dinner.
places.desk_note: The phone number comes from the Michelin Guide; its own site lists none. Its hours are printed without AM or PM and read here as evening.

places.name: Angler

hours.tue: 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM
hours.wed: 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM
hours.thu: 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM
hours.fri: 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM
hours.sat: 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM

places.hours_note: Golden Hour Tuesday to Saturday, 5:00 to 6:30 PM.
places.description: A wood-fired seafood restaurant on the Embarcadero waterfront where nearly every dish is touched by the hearth. A top choice for a special dinner or a business lunch with bay views, a short walk from the East Cut.
places.desk_note: Its site still carries last winter's notices, so the hours may be stale. Confirm by phone.

places.name: Quince

hours.fri: Lunch 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM; dinner, reservations 5:00 to 8:00 PM
hours.sat: Lunch 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM; dinner, reservations 5:00 to 8:00 PM

places.hours_note: Bolinas Bar seats walk-ins first come, first served. Closed Nov 26 and Dec 25 to 26; open Christmas Eve lunch and New Year's Eve dinner.
places.description: Michael Tusk's three-star Jackson Square restaurant, an ever-changing menu built on ingredients from its own Fresh Run Farm. The pick for the most serious special-occasion dinner within a short ride of downtown.
places.desk_note: The times are when tables can be booked, not when it closes. The bar seats walk-ins.

places.name: Saison
places.hours_note: Bar Experience Tue to Thu, walk-ins welcome when seats are free. Dinner reservations release by the 1st of the prior month.
places.description: A two-star tasting-menu restaurant in SoMa with a dedicated wine program and an optional bar experience. A strong choice for a long, elegant dinner in SoMa.
places.desk_note: No closing time is published. Confirm the schedule by phone.

places.name: Lazy Bear
places.hours_note: Dinner seating by ticket; no phone reservations.
places.description: A two-star tasting-menu dinner in the Mission, sold as tickets for set seatings. A strong special-occasion night out for a group.
places.desk_note: Sold as tickets on Tock for set seatings. No phone reservations.

places.name: Cotogna
places.hours_note: Closed Thursday, November 26 (Thanksgiving).
places.description: A rustic Italian dining room a short walk from the Financial District, known for hand-rolled pasta, rotisserie meats and a wood-fired oven. A dependable choice for a polished but relaxed dinner or a weekday lunch.
places.desk_note: Books by phone or email; the buttons on its site do not work.

places.name: Perbacco
places.hours_note: Site says Monday service opens in December.
places.description: A long-running Financial District Italian restaurant focused on the cooking of Piedmont, with house-made pasta and cured meats. Convenient for a business lunch or a dinner before an evening downtown.
places.desk_note: Closed Mondays for now. Its site says Monday service returns in December.

places.name: Delfina
places.description: A neighborhood Italian restaurant in the Mission that has been a local standard for simple, well-made Tuscan-leaning cooking, including its signature spaghetti. Good when you want an unfussy, lively dinner outside downtown.

places.name: A16
places.hours_note: This listing is the Chestnut Street restaurant, not the Ferry Building counter.
places.description: A Southern Italian restaurant with a wood-fired pizza oven and a strong pasta and wine program, centered on Campania. A lively, good-value choice for a group dinner.
places.desk_note: Two numbers are in circulation. This is the one on its own site.

places.name: EPIC Steak
places.hours_note: Weekend brunch Sat and Sun 11:30 AM to 2:30 PM. Happy hour Mon to Fri 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM.
places.description: A steakhouse on the Embarcadero waterfront with bay views, serving prime cuts and seafood. A natural pick for a client dinner or celebration close to the East Cut.

places.name: Alexander's Steakhouse
places.address: 165 O'Farrell Street, 3rd Floor, San Francisco, CA 94102
places.hours_note: Closed Nov 26, Dec 25, 2026 and Jan 1, 2027.
places.description: A luxury steakhouse on an upper floor near Union Square, known for Wagyu and Japanese-influenced touches. Suited to a special-occasion dinner.
places.desk_note: Holiday hours conflict on its site. Confirm by phone near a holiday.

places.name: Niku Steakhouse
places.description: A Japanese-influenced steakhouse in SoMa focused on high-grade Wagyu, with a tasting-style approach to the meal. A strong choice for a serious steak dinner with a Michelin-recognized kitchen.

places.name: Waterbar
places.hours_note: Lunch 11:30 AM to 2:15 PM; bar menu 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM; dinner from 5:00 PM. No valet parking.
places.description: A seafood restaurant under the Bay Bridge with floor-to-ceiling views and a large fish tank, serving oysters and sustainably sourced fish. One of the closest good seafood rooms to 181 Fremont.

places.name: Tadich Grill
places.hours_note: Sunday closed to regular dining (buyouts only). Walk-ins seated first come, first served.
places.description: The city's old-school grill, in business since the 1800s, with a counter, booths and classics like cioppino and sand dabs. A true San Francisco experience for visiting family or colleagues.

places.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
places.hours_note: No reservations; casual dine-in and oysters to go.
places.description: A casual oyster bar inside the Ferry Building with bay views, serving oysters from its own farm, chowder and grilled cheese. Best for a quick, high-quality seafood meal or a drink on the waterfront.

places.name: Wayfare Tavern
places.description: Tyler Florence's tavern in a handsome Financial District space, known for popovers and buttermilk fried chicken. Reliable for client lunches and dinners within a few blocks of downtown offices.
places.desk_note: Moved to 201 Pine Street in 2025; older guides still show Sacramento Street. Its site looks dated, so confirm hours by phone.

places.name: Zuni Cafe

hours.sat: 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM
hours.sun: 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM

places.hours_note: Last seating 9:30 PM. Closed Nov 26, Dec 24, 25 and 31. Parties of 7 or more must call.
places.description: A long-standing Market Street restaurant famous for its wood-oven roast chicken with bread salad and its oysters. A classic San Francisco meal that suits a leisurely lunch or dinner.

places.hours_note: Lunch Tuesday to Friday, dinner Tuesday to Saturday. On Folsom between First and Fremont.
places.description: A long-running sushi counter that now sits a few steps from Fremont Street, serving omakase at lunch and dinner. Its early, tightly timed service and focus on nigiri suit a resident who wants a serious sushi meal close to home.
places.desk_note: Does not take or change reservations by phone. Parties over four book by email.

places.hours_note: Happy hour Monday to Saturday 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM. Lunch is Monday to Friday. A separate sake bar, Pabu-Chan, opened beside it in November 2025.
places.description: A Michael Mina izakaya in the 101 California tower, built around shared small plates and sushi with a sake list to match. An easy, polished choice for a weekday lunch or a group dinner near the Embarcadero.
places.desk_note: Hours are from the owner group's page. Other sites show a later closing; confirm by phone.

places.name: Kusakabe
places.hours_note: Two fixed seatings, Tuesday to Sunday. Reservation line is staffed Tuesday to Sunday 12:30 PM to 4:00 PM. A credit card is required to hold a table.
places.description: An omakase sushi counter near Chinatown and the Financial District, with a full multi-course menu and a shorter petite option. Suits a quiet, focused sushi dinner for a small party.
places.desk_note: Two seatings a night, nothing between. The reservation line is staffed Tuesday to Sunday, 12:30 to 4:00 PM.

places.name: Yank Sing
places.hours_note: Daytime only.
places.description: A family-run dim sum house a few blocks from 181 Fremont, with a daytime-only service of dumplings and small plates. A dependable choice for a business lunch or a weekend family meal.
places.desk_note: The Rincon Center room has closed. Stevenson Street is the only location now.

places.name: Mister Jiu's
places.hours_note: Dinner only. Tock bookings open 30 days ahead at 10 AM Pacific; a per-guest deposit is required and credited to the bill.
places.description: Brandon Jew's Chinatown dining room, where Cantonese banquet cooking meets Californian produce. A strong pick for a celebration or when guests want a Chinese meal with some ceremony.
places.desk_note: Books on Tock only, never by phone or email. The phone number comes from the Michelin Guide.

places.hours_note: At the corner of Mason and Ellis Streets, in the Parc 55 hotel. Lunch daily; dinner to 9:00 PM Sunday to Thursday, 10:00 PM Friday and Saturday.
places.description: Pim Techamuanvivit's Thai restaurant, known for bold regional cooking that does not tone down the heat. Good for guests who want a lively, flavorful dinner or a quick serious lunch.

places.name: San Ho Won
places.hours_note: Closed Thanksgiving Day and the Friday after. Reservations release at 10:00 AM, 29 days ahead.
places.description: A Korean charcoal-grill restaurant from Corey Lee's team, centered on tabletop barbecue and home-style dishes. Worth the ride to the Mission for a group that wants a lively, high-quality dinner.

places.description: A Peruvian restaurant on the Embarcadero waterfront, known for ceviche and pisco drinks. A bright, easy place for lunch by the bay or a relaxed dinner.

places.hours_note: Phone reservations taken daily 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Reservations open 30 days ahead.
places.description: A Spanish tapas restaurant on Pier 5, with a grill and a long list of small plates for sharing. Good for a group that wants a long, casual meal on the water.
